title: Hosted API composability PRD — acceptance matrix and scope change log
creator: Asha Menon
description: This PRD defines requirements, acceptance criteria, and a scoped launch checklist for a composability-first Hosted API surface that standardizes how chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints can be composed into single request flows and deterministic consumer contracts. The goal is to enable multi-step interactions without bespoke orchestration in client code while keeping latency, cost, and behavioral guarantees predictable for production applications.
goals: Provide a minimal composable payload format that supports chained calls across chat, completion, embedding, and rerank in a single API invocation
Define deterministic behavioral contracts and a per-endpoint acceptance matrix to avoid regressions when models or kernels change
Ship an eval-gated canary rollout with telemetry and automated regression alerts before broad launch
Document compatibility rules for Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private and versioning expectations
non_goals: Full orchestration engine (we will not ship stateful orchestration or long-running workflows in this phase)
Native multi-turn retrieval augmentation beyond basic embedding lookup — advanced RAG pipelines deferred to a later phase
Major SDK language expansions (initial SDK surface limited to JS and Python)
success_metrics: Acceptable P50 end-to-end latency for composed requests: <= 450ms for 95% of small payloads
No more than 1 quality regression per 10k composed requests as measured by eval prompt set within 2 weeks of rollout
< 3% increase in token cost compared to equivalent sequential calls after batching/kv optimizations
> 90% of internal integration tests pass across host/dedicated/private compatibility matrix pre-launch
acceptance_criteria: Contract: A documented composable request schema with required fields for intent, step definitions, and deterministic seed/temperature semantics
Per-endpoint behavior matrix populated: chat, completions, embeddings, rerank rows with expected input/output invariants
Backward compatibility: Single-version adapter for existing clients; stable defaults preserve prior behavior unless caller opts into composable mode
Quality gate: Eval harness with > 100 representative composability test cases, automated daily runs and blocking threshold configured
Operational: Console telemetry for composed requests (end-to-end latency, per-step latency, token counts, error reasons) visible in staged account
Canary rollout plan documented with traffic slices, automatic abort thresholds (latency/quality/error rate), and rollback playbook
Security: KMS keys honored for composed payloads in Private and Dedicated flavors; audit logs capture step-level decision metadata
SDK: High-level helpers for building composable payloads in JS and Python with examples for common patterns (QA -> rerank, summarize -> embed -> index)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 — Internal alpha: feature gated for Redwood internal orgs, run through end-to-end integration tests (2 weeks)
Phase 1 — Beta: opt-in customers by invitation, 1% production traffic for 1 week, monitor metrics and eval regressions
Phase 2 — Gradual launch: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 48h observation windows and automatic abort on threshold breaches
Automated fallback: requests that fail composable processing fall back to sequential endpoint calls preserving caller semantics
Communication: release notes, migration guide, and SDK sample repo published at beta launch
launch_checklist: PRD sign-off by PM, Eng, Design, Security
Acceptance matrix completed and green for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
Canary dashboard with composed-request panels created in Console
Eval harness stable with baseline test results and alerting thresholds configured
SDK packages released with examples and migration guide
Documentation: composable request schema, behavioral guarantees, error codes, and best practices published
Support runbook & FAQ created for SRE and Solutions teams
Legal and compliance review completed for telemetry and audit logging behavior
dependencies: ENG-98321: Runtime batching primitives to support multi-step fused execution
ENG-100112: KV cache exposure for per-step reuse across composed requests
PM-402911: Eval dataset creation for composability scenarios
DES-540: UX flows for composable request builder in Console
risks: Composed requests could magnify model nondeterminism and surface regressions that are harder to attribute to a single step
Latency tail risk when steps cannot be efficiently batched together across heterogeneous model architectures
Increased billing complexity for customers who expect per-step metering; need clear cost breakdowns
Behavioral drift when runtime kernel swaps or quantization changes are rolled out without synchronized acceptance testing
migration_plan: Provide migration guide: how to convert existing sequential flows to the composable payload (examples included)
Compatibility adapter on server-side that accepts older endpoint calls and converts to composable flow where safe
Deprecation policy: no automatic removal for 12 months; telemetry will surface active legacy usage before any deprecation notice
Customer outreach: targeted emails and in-console banners for accounts using >100k sequential composed-equivalent calls/month
notes: Decision: composable payload will be opt-in by default; explicit header X-Redwood-Composable: true required
Trade-off: tighter behavioral guarantees require constrained defaults (temp=0.2, top_p fixed) which customers can override at cost of reproducibility
We will not support arbitrary user-defined plugins in phase 1; only built-in step types for the four endpoint kinds
